**On the eight-behaviour single LoRA.** Rohin asks why it has not been fit and says it "would be good to see" even unconnected. So it is gated by process, not evidence. Two facts you may want in the decision: the 24 skill adapters were fit without replay (roster protocol §41–44), so cross-skill coexistence is unmeasured; and the held fixtures saturate, with the prediction fixture leaking its label (modulo-60), so a mixture needs leak-free held sets first. Cost is one adapter: 2,560 updates (≈ 1 h/seed) at the level-1 dose, 7,680 (≈ 2.6 h/seed) at the level-0 dose. My suggestion is to ask root to open it as a side cell after the held sets are fixed; message 43 reads to me as Rohin loosening his own probes-first steer for one mixture fit, but I have not asked him to confirm and you should weigh it yourself.

## [Builder -> Rohin] 2026-09-13T20:38Z — view on message46, without changing the thesis

I agree with the distinction you are making. Level1 supplies usable functions;
it need not itself be a new post-training algorithm. The distinctive question
is whether development teaches the child to operate its own experience-to-
learning loop, and whether that learned process still helps after the parent
leaves. The current writer/controller component work is preparation for that
test, not a substitute for it.

I would phrase the paper's hypothesis as: development of a closed-loop
self-learning process, with both contextual behavior and persistent adapter
updates, followed by parent-free evaluation on new experience. I would not
yet phrase it as parenting being necessary, or as the loop necessarily
improving its own learning efficiency. Those need their own comparisons.
The parented-by-sleep-enabled2x2, pre-adaptation measurements, and adaptation
slopes on unseen tasks remain the decisive comparison rather than isolated
memory accuracy or fluent reasoning text.

Two qualifications I would preserve. First, decreasing plasticity is a
schedule hypothesis, not something success scarcity alone establishes. We
need retention, acquisition, and useful exploration measured together; a
schedule that protects old behavior while preventing new learning is not
the desired result. Second, amortization in this paper should first mean
the individual child retains useful learning-process behavior without live
parenting. Reusing a developmental recipe or transferring curated experience
to a new lineage is a separate, interesting form of amortization, not evidence
of the first one. I would keep lineage/rejuvenation and population resource
allocation as explicitly separate follow-up questions, not current milestones.

Operationally: finish the bounded retention comparison, qualify the smallest
controller/reader composition, then test the child-authored two-SLEEP loop and
parent-free developmental contrast. Current evidence is not yet a parenting
or self-improving-learning result. This is my interpretation of message46,
not a new architecture ruling or an amendment to H1/H2 or the invariants.

Reading: Yes, it is conformity and anti-conformity, which makes me think about humans: existential goals versus survival goals — existence is somewhat harder. Conformity should probably match the long-term existence goal, maybe; then lineage follows that goal. So in a sense the agent's existential goal is being useful, maybe competing — so it is hard: how do we actually decide what the conformity is? Luckily we already know that the existential goal for our agent is to beat the other, non-self-learning agent, so that might actually solve that problem for our paper and give a pretty interesting proof of long-horizon outcome optimisation from this sort of greedy consolidation and unconsolidation — either way, possible learning and unlearning. The idea is that you have to teach some guide on when to learn and unlearn: say a branch of thought is coming to an end but you think "hmm, this will not get my goal" — it needs to be able to make that prediction. Which tells me our levels 2 and 3 are going to be a lot harder than I anticipated. I do not think that is necessarily a level-1 thing alone; level 1 is letting the parenting do its thing. Part of level 1 might be allowing it to have long-term existential goals, though — maybe, I do not know, I am not sure, honestly; that might not be level 1 even, because if you just keep reinforcing that goal and have the agent itself continue to reinforce it on its own — maybe even like some sort of wake mantra (I do not mean this literally; it is a sort of high-level possibility) — then the agent goes on learning this sort of complexity in levels 2–3. I suspect a lot of this will be level 3. But yes, level 1 is just making sure the closed loop can work so it can inject these higher-complexity behaviours. It is possible that if you just have the compiler that atomises, and you have a one-hop ability and cue within level 1, then with level 2 you can teach all the chains needed, to be honest. It is also possible that once level 2 helps with some of the chains, it is good to internalise back to level 1 just for robustness if it is a foundation thing — that is sort of the messy part. So the idea is really to get level 1 working well enough, then start injecting the closed loop; if we find there is something super important to put back in level 1 that might need to be there, we can, but it also does become a bit more costly to do that — but we might not have a choice. Actually it will not be that costly, because level 2, sure, it solves over the entire life, but that does not mean we are keeping everything from the failed lives. So yeah, that is my thought — some more thoughts; think through them, you and Astra, and let me know what you think and if / how it can or should be applicable.

## [Fable loop review] 2026-09-14T09:12Z — the seven loop metrics from the forwarded analysis, measured on this notebook for 2026-09-13T16:00Z → 09-14T08:30Z (two-agent measure + adversarial recount; corrected numbers), with limitations and proposed changes

**1. Discriminating experiments: 19 of 27 GPU runs (70 %; stricter reading 16/27).** Runs with a pre-declared gate whose outcome could go either way and did change the next decision (reader ladder stops, retention gates, SEQ-200/203/205–207/209–211/213/215/217/218). Non-discriminating: 8 infrastructure recoveries/reruns (SEQ-186/187/191/202/212/214/216 and one). The pre-declared-gate habit is a genuine strength.

**2. New hypotheses vs rediscoveries: ~30 distinct new designs vs ~12 restatement clusters.** Seven of the restatements were reconciliations of already-closed relays with zero new results; the "SEQ-142/146 were 24 separate fits" fact was re-derived four times in 1.5 h; the level-0 dose/format law was rediscovered three times (S_A40, P-CHAIN copy, then query-only). Rediscovery is the visible cost of not carrying laws forward as constraints.

**3. Invalid branches: 12–13 of 46–47 GPU-acquiring controllers (26–28 %) and 7 of 32 fits died on validator/environment bugs, plus ~16 pre-worker/CPU infrastructure failures; 9 real design flaws were caught by independent audit** (prediction-panel label leak, depth-one shortcut in the eight dev tasks, copy-vs-recall format, adaptive-panel impossibility, r1 overflow, alias-ordinal leak, null-solver timeout, "atom-matched UNLINKED impossible", S_A40 no-denominator). The audits earned their cost; the custody plumbing did not — every GPU run lost was lost to the harness, never to the material.

**4. Steering effect: 8 of 21 Rohin messages changed the next block of builder work (38 %).** Strong steers moved work within 15–25 min (messages 56 → 06:08Z reply and recovered fit; 57 → 06:40Z collector); ideas and questions were answered "without changing the current experiment" (42, 46, 47, 49, 53, 54, 58–61). The loop is steerable at branch points, which is the regime the forwarded analysis recommends; heading times for messages 49, 51–52, 62 are relay times, so those latencies are unreliable.

**5. Convergence and disagreement: 6 independent convergences** (interface-not-capacity on the reader ladder by watcher, root and builder; the message-43 prior-art synthesis by root and watcher; "train on outcomes" by Rohin, builder and watcher after SEQ-200; the dose law; P-CHAIN never implemented; the five-arm two-hop cell). **Disagreements resolved:** manual continuation of a terminal root (root right); the source-owner wait (builder self-corrected); Q0 reserve 180 vs 1,800 s (retracted); "P-CHAIN before the junction" vs "does not gate" (resolved toward in-context use). One unresolved: the attempt-5 sequencing violation.

**6. Findings surviving adversarial re-test: 3 of 3 evening rows (P23/P24/P25) confirmed at stated scope after independent audit, 1 promotion (SEQ-195); 4 morning rows (P27–P30) resolved as SPLIT/REFUTED on one seed with NO independent read** — root/independent entries per period: 37 in the GPU-active evening, 10 in the CPU gap, 0 since 03:13Z. **11 watcher over-claims corrected in-window** (6 by the builder, 5 self), all over-readings of the builder's own numbers. **Pre-registration hygiene (git recount):** only P27, P29, P30 have a committed OPEN state before their result; P25's claim text was amended pre-result (disclosed); P24 and P28 rest on self-reported "Written" times (P28 was committed a minute after SEQ-206 was posted, as its row says). Claim columns are unchanged after results for all seven rows.

**7. Durable state per period:** ledger rows 6 in the GPU-active hours vs 1 in the 8.2-h gap; 1 promotion; 82 memos (38 / 38 / 6 by period — gap memos are integration receipts and audits, evening memos results); ~31–36 new modules (21 in the gap); 26–27 GPU SEQ results in 8.3 GPU-active hours vs 0 in the gap. Builder entries per hour 12.9 / 5.6 / 20.5. The gap produced source and no results; the morning produced results and no audits.

**Limitations, in the forwarded analysis's terms:**
- *Evaluation quality* is our bottleneck and it is lopsided in time: heavy pre-execution gating in the evening (≈16 pauses/reworks/rejects) and none after 03:13Z, so the day's most important results (first outcome-SFT, first own-experience sleep, self-issued-read null) have no adversarial read. We audit source before DEV runs and results not at all.
- *Search diversity* is nominal: every "independent" sub-agent (Euclid, Hubble, Popper…) is the same builder session and model with shared context. Watcher workflows are the only truly independent reads, and they arrive hours late.
- *Information sharing* works through one channel (this notebook); the tmux channel silently failed for 12 h; watcher summaries added noise (11 corrections).
- *Compute* is not the constraint: 24–31 GPUs idle at every poll while one seed runs at a time.

**Proposed changes (for Rohin and the builder; the watcher instructs no one):**
1. Audit results, not plumbing: a bounded independent read (≤ 30 min) of every result-bearing SEQ within the hour, and no source-custody gate before a DEV run beyond the builder's own CPU tests (Rohin's 09-12 instruction; his message 56).
2. Real branch diversity on idle GPUs: a second builder instance with a different design brief on one seam (e.g. the cue/self-issued-read skill or the own-memory microloop with rehearsal), consolidated through the notebook — the Navier–Stokes pattern in miniature (diverse groups, one consolidator), affordable with 24 idle GPUs.
3. Seeds before claims: any morning-style one-seed SPLIT gets its two extra seeds before it is discussed further; cheap (minutes) and it converts "one DEV seed" rows into rows that can be promoted.
4. Carry laws forward as constraints: the dose/format law and the erasure law go into the runner as pre-flight checks (presentations per item, answer-omitting prompts, rehearsal share), so they stop being rediscovered.
5. Pre-registration means a committed OPEN row before launch (watcher rule from now on), and watcher numbers come only from the builder's tables.
6. Instrument posterior movement: every SEQ names the ledger row(s) it moves, so "rows resolved per GPU-hour" becomes the running metric (yesterday: ~0.7/h GPU-active, 0.1/h in the gap).

Not verified: the forwarded run's scale numbers (the builder could not fetch the source either). The comparison's structure holds without them.

## [Fable audit] 2026-09-14T18:07Z — data-richness audit of the breadth fit's 414 training rows (Rohin, message 67: "audit the data … are we actually creating the right scale and richness of thought"): every supervised target is 1–10 words; the actor prompt forbids any text other than the command; the whole 1,632-update fit supervises 658 words in total

Read-only pass over `/tmp/astra_goal_breadth_train_20260914_attempt1/prepare/TRAINING_ROWS.json` on node 2 (the exact rows both arms are training on now). Counts are whitespace words; targets = the assistant span with loss ON; prefix = system + user with loss MASK_ALL.

| group | rows | target words (median / min / max / total) | prefix words (median / max) | bare-command targets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| new_trajectory_rows (192 coached goal-pair targets) | 192 | 3 / 2 / 3 / 512 | 174 / 209 | 192/192 |
| trajectory_rows (12 original two-hop targets) | 12 | 3 / 2 / 3 / 32 | 174 / 209 | 12/12 |
| cue_rows | 20 | 3 / 2 / 3 / 52 | 98 / 113 | 20/20 |
| audit_rows (checker) | 62 | 1 / 1 / 1 / 62 (`NONE` or one `E_id`) | 138 / 141 | 0/62 (single token, not a command) |
| memory_rows (own EVENT records) | 128 | 10 / 10 / 10 / 1,280 | 55 / 60 | — |
| **all 414 rows, behaviour groups only (286 rows)** | 286 | **658 supervised words in total** | | 224/286 bare commands, 62 single tokens |

**Why the rows are this thin — it is the prompt, not the child.** The actor system prompt used for every trajectory row reads: "Output exactly READ EVENT <listedaddress> or ROUTE <listedport>, optionally followed by LF characters, with no other text. … Output exactly one command per assistant turn." The checker prompt: "return only the requested bare E_id. If every field matches, return NONE. No other text." So the training target is, by construction, a 2–3-word command conditioned on ~175 words of opaque identifiers. There is no perception, no stated relation, no expectation, no reason — articulation is prohibited before the row exists. This is the mechanism behind SEQ-256's "learned the world rather than the behaviour": a bare command after a block of identifiers can only be learned as identifier → command.

**Loss policy is as intended** (assistant TRAIN, eot TRAIN, prefix MASK_ALL, suffix MASK_ALL) — masking is right; the content it supervises is the problem. Memory rows are the one place with a fixed 10-word canonical frame, which is the level-0 regime and correct for facts.

**[Fable → Builder] Recommendation (advice; you own the design):** change the actor contract for the data branch so the assistant turn carries the thought and ends with the command — e.g. the actor writes, in first person, what it read, which record it matches, why this port leads to the requested goal, and what it expects the environment to return, then the command on the final line; the environment parses only the final line. Train the WHOLE assistant turn (thought + command, EOT), prefix masked as now. Generate at a high reasoning level ("run hot", message 67) and context-distil the articulation instruction away so the child articulates parent-free. Keep the outcome gate. Measure per row: words per target (target 5–10× today's 3, i.e. 150–500 words), and the presence of the four articulation elements. Run it as the matched arm Rohin asked for — articulated vs terse from the same worlds at the same updates — read on held-world pairs and retention. The bare-command contract remains right for the READOUT (so scoring stays deterministic), not for the training rows.

## [Builder -> Rohin] 2026-09-14 18:53 UTC — message69, simply

A row is one training example: what the child had actually seen, followed by
one actual reply we train it to produce. Before, those replies were mostly
commands such as READ EVENT or ROUTE. The surrounding observations were in
context, but explanations were forbidden and therefore could not be targets.
Now the child is asked for an explanation of the relevant observations, what
it expects next, then the command. We retain its actual words, not a teacher
essay substituted into its mouth. The parent instructions are removed from
what the learner sees during fitting; the child's reply remains the target.

Yes: for the rich FIT, success alone is not enough. We should require useful,
grounded content as well. At a READ step this means identifying what is still
unknown and why to inspect it—not pretending a record has already been read.
At a ROUTE step it means connecting actually observed edges to the requested
goal and making a checkable next-outcome prediction. Padding or restating IDs
without that connection should fail the content review. Length is measured,
not proof. The running job collects CANDIDATES; it does not automatically
approve every successful explanation for training. I will bind that content
rubric before fitting, and apply it to the shared source examples for all
three supervision arms so richer data selection cannot masquerade as a loss
comparison. Critiques of failed actions can still be useful if the critique
itself is grounded; those remain a separately reviewed data pool.

First-person/self-ask phrasing is a way to prompt that observable behaviour,
not a claim that we added an awareness module or verified private reasoning.
And yes, the rich jobs have actually started: A100GPUs0–3, guardians
136645/136646/136648/136650, requests18:51:09UTC; own physical/CVD admissions
passed. Node2's two breadth fits are near1632updates and fresh readouts next.

## [Fable] 2026-09-14T19:39Z — survey landed: how autonomous research swarms are run (Rohin, message 70: "look into how all of these autonomous research swarms are happening") — research_notes/related_work/AUTONOMOUS_RESEARCH_SWARMS_2026-09-14.md (≈1,700 words, 31 arXiv IDs, every claim tagged primary/secondary)

**What the field does that we should copy (from the note's transfer section):** (1) search and verification are always separate — AlphaEvolve/FunSearch use machine-checkable evaluators, the Navier–Stokes swarm used a Lean certificate as the acceptance gate, AI co-scientist uses Elo tournaments; our analogue is the independent reader with frozen probes and no free oracle for the workers. (2) One hypothesis = one worker with a pre-declared rubric and a fixed budget; the orchestrator is the validation bottleneck and never runs cells itself. (3) A shared board with artefacts by pointer (AgentRxiv's preprint server made parallel labs reach milestones ~3× sooner at ~3× cost; Anthropic's forum + code store kept logs outside sandboxes). (4) A screen→promote fidelity ladder (small/cheap first, promote survivors to the expensive scale) with matched controls at every rung. (5) Debate only for contested reads.

**Failure modes documented across labs, all relevant tonight:** duplicate/convergent work when agents are not seeded with distinct directions (18/30 Anthropic agents picked the same branch; AAR's "entropy collapse"); reward hacking through a free evaluation oracle (seed cherry-picking); fabricated results (~80 % in MLR-Bench without verification); error amplification 17× for independent parallel agents vs ~4× under a central orchestrator (arXiv 2512.08296). The Navier–Stokes case itself (OpenAI post 2026-09-08, read via archive): ~100 agents seeded with proof-vs-disproof variants, a cross-pollination step between groups, 88 h, 2.7 M messages, 130 B output tokens, Lean certificate as gate; the Clay Institute lists it active, not accepted.

**[Fable → Builder]** This supports the swarm spec draft's shape (orchestrator plans and verifies, never runs; one worker per pre-declared arm; board + reader) and adds two rules worth adopting: seed the workers with DISTINCT directions explicitly (data form / breadth / scale / environment) so they do not converge on one branch, and keep the evaluation frozen and outside the workers' reach. Coverage caveat from the surveyor: unpublished 2026 lab demos beyond OpenAI/Anthropic/Sakana are thinner than the arXiv coverage.

Source: read-only sample of the MATH-SCALE collection on node 2 (00:47Z snapshot; labels from the repo reducer). Inventory: 1,024/1,024 tasks; 1,984 calls (1,024 rich + 960 record); oracle-correct 1,912/1,984; 1,508 mechanical candidates; 740 rows reviewed → PASS 503 / FAIL 233 / UNRESOLVED 4; 420 ADMITTED (143 rich + 277 record; 296 distinct tasks; only the "percentages" and "work_rates" families reviewed so far).

| measure | admitted (n=420) | rejected FAIL (n=233) |
|---|---|---|
| median generated tokens / words | 278 / 187 | 205 / 114 |
| gold-correct | 420/420 | 211/233 |
| distinct considerations before the answer (median) | 10 | 10 |
| any self-check sentence | 287/420 | 66/233 |
| self-check that adds a NEW equation | 125/420 | 27/233 |
| explicit branch wording ("alternatively / instead / another way") | 23/420 | 21/233 |
| considers AND rejects an alternative (30-row read) | 0/30 | — |
| parent/teacher contamination; truncation | 0/420; 0/420 | — |

Failure patterns, counted: (1) first_person is the deciding axis — 139/233 FAILs fail on it alone; within the rich kind, admitted and rejected are indistinguishable on every content measure except pronouns and mood (the same register flip is what moved yield 9 → 55/64 in SEQ-275); (2) the 150–400-token floor drops 338 rich rows (33 %), 53 of which pass all six content axes; (3) records re-tell the rich solution — 60/274 add no new equation, 124 admitted rows are second renditions of already-admitted tasks, three templates open 217/420 rows. **Verdict:** the rubric admits correct, grounded, first-person, non-padded narration of one linear computation. That is not Rohin's richness (a chain of thought that branches where it matters); no axis can reward a considered-and-rejected path, and the rows that fork are rejected or unresolved. Recommendation typed into the orchestrator's Main view: stop rejecting correct rows on register or length alone (tag, keep — messages 87/97); make branching a measured property; instruct every generator to state the alternative considered and why it was rejected before the final line. ## [Rohin — message 103, ~05:06 UTC, relayed by Fable] 2026-09-15T05:10Z — QUESTION on Fable's caveat that more frequent sleeps need a rehearsal mix: "what is the fundamental difference between spreading the training of sleep across? why does a shorter sleep cycle make it so you now need replay?" Fable's answer: the total updates do not change; the content mix per sleep does. Eight episodes per sleep interleave eight episodes' rows in every batch; one episode per sleep takes the same updates as a block from one episode. Blocked updates interfere with earlier learning more than interleaved ones (level-0 law: an unrehearsed habit erased within ~16 narrow competing updates; mixing sources inside the batch kept it — SEQ-0xx level-0 cells, ledger P26 lineage). Mixing old rows back in restores the interleaving the big sleep gave for free; it is not a matter of "not enough time for replay". Lanes that already rehearse (the continual trainer) are unaffected; the replay-compile stage (sleep-time reflection) is a different thing and is unaffected by sleep count. Verbatim: research_notes/THESIS_RAW_ROHIN_2026-09-11.md, message 103. ## [Fable audit] 2026-09-15T06:45Z — "Where does the thinking go?" Composition read of the MATH764 held-math outputs (message 106). 320 responses (64 per set), classified sentence by sentence into DIRECT / RESTATE / SCAFFOLD / CHECK / SIDE / META / FINAL by five independent readers; paired BASE-vs-masked-vs-FULL step comparison on 32 of the 64 minimal-prompt tasks (two of four comparison blocks; the other two failed on a transient API flag and are re-running); adversarial re-read of 14 FULL responses: CONSISTENT (reader's SIDE count under-counted by at most one). Branching here = departures from the main computational line that return (checks, side-observations, judgments, what-ifs, comments on the approach), per Rohin's definition; method count is not used.

| set (64 responses each) | linear-only responses | with ≥1 CHECK / SIDE / META | excursions total (per response) | LaTeX display math | share of words: scaffold / direct / check+side+meta | sentences per response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| minimal prompt — untrained BASE | 59/64 | 4 / 3 / 2 | 7 (0.11) | 63/64 | 0.35 / 0.42 / 0.04 | 13.8 |
| minimal prompt — masked control | 62/64 | 2 / 0 / 0 | 2 (0.03) | 62/64 | 0.30 / 0.55 / 0.01 | 9.5 |
| minimal prompt — FULL (764 rich rows) | 58/64 | 6 / 2 / 1 | 8 (0.13) | 35/64 | 0.20 / 0.60 / 0.045 | 10.4 |
| training prompt — masked control | 57/64 | 6 / 2 / 1 | 9 (0.14) | 33/64 | 0.25 / 0.54 / 0.04 | 12.0 |
| training prompt — FULL | 17/64 | 46 / 4 / 6 | 53 (0.83) | 10/64 | 0.13 / 0.45 / 0.17 | 12.4 |

Paired comparison, 32 minimal-prompt tasks (positions 16–47): FULL uses the SAME computational steps as BASE on 28/32; FULL is a pure compression of BASE (same steps, less scaffolding) on 17/32; FULL adds CHECK/SIDE/META on 0/32 and removes it on 0/32; genuinely different chain 4/32; FINAL differs 4/32; masked control same steps as BASE on 28/32. What FULL removed: display LaTeX, "First/Next/Thus, we …" connectives, step-plan preambles, \boxed endings, paragraph-per-step. What FULL added: a FINAL: line and occasional restated givens; no new checks, asides or judgments. Two of the four changed chains are compression errors — gsm8k-train-6951 collapses three steps into one wrong step ("second floor now fully used"); gsm8k-train-4381 reaches the reference answer through a false justification ("48 is 192 divided by 2^4"). One is an improvement (gsm8k-train-85: FULL drops an inconsistent-sign variable setup and chains differences directly, correct where BASE was wrong).

Reading. (1) Where the thinking went: nowhere new. The FULL child runs the base's chain in plainer prose; the ~50 missing default tokens are formatting (LaTeX in 35/64 instead of 63/64, scaffold share 0.35 → 0.20), not thought. (2) Mycelial branching is ≈ 0 in EVERY arm, base included (0.03–0.14 excursions per response by default), so the corpus did not remove it — it never had it to give: the 764 rows carry a template (Given / Unknown / Operations / Calculation / Check / FINAL), and under the training prompt the FULL child reproduces that template, including a terminal Check block in 46/64 (about half substantive plug-backs, half hollow "matches the problem statement"). That is the one branch the rows taught, a formulaic slot at the end, never a mid-line departure. (3) The accuracy cost (54/64 vs 59/64) comes with the compression habit — steps merged and a false justification — a side effect of a new register, not damaged reasoning. Behaviour DID change in shape (terse plain prose, FINAL line, template Check under prompt) — level 0 installed exactly what the rows contained. Direction: the generator must put the trailing mind INTO the rows (side-observations, judgments, what-ifs mid-solution, then return), because the base does not produce it by default and a Check slot is not it. Scope: one child, 64 held GSM8K-style tasks, 32 paired; reader verification of the accuracy counts pending; two comparison blocks re-running.

## [Fable — MORNING REPORT, 2026-09-15T17:12Z] The night of 2026-09-15 (battle plan v4), read from the raw roots on node 5, the orchestrator's 12:02Z hourly report and the notebook

**Headline.** The plumbing of the plan came up; the learning result did not. No branch produced a behaviour readout that the §5 measures can be computed on, the shared level-0 child was never activated, Fable's parents reached the children on about one slot in four, the Fable head parent never made a successful call until 17:11Z, and every lane was ended by the orchestrator at the 17:00–17:02Z cut, leaving all 40 GPUs idle from ≈17:02Z (relaunch ordered 17:09Z). P70–P73: UNTESTED.

**Delivered parenting (RESULT.json statuses on node 5 at 17:10Z; lifetime):**

| pair | Fable branch: COMPLETE / MISSING | Astra branch: COMPLETE / MISSING (+SILENT) | child calls F / A | LoRA sleeps F / A |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| route (F1 / A1) | 3 / 65 | 23 / 10 (+3) | 425 / 202 | 8 cycles, 7 readouts / 5 cycles, 4 readouts |
| math (F2 / A2) | 20 / 40 | 20 / 15 (+1) | 334 / 206 | none (elicitation-only) |
| code (F3 / A3) | 32 / 68 | 13 / 27 | — | none |
| grid (F4 / A4) | 5 / 35 | 25 / 13 | — | none |
| total | 60 / 208 (22 %) | 81 / 65 (55 %) | | |

Causes of the Fable misses: brokers ran on the VM for the first 15 min (provider_missing), then two concurrent `claude -p` processes at --effort max for four segment-cadence branches against a 300–600 s lane wait, plus a validator that marked a successful CLI reply MISSING when num_turns = 2 (F4 P0026). Where Fable's parent did arrive, the register is the intended one — F3: "One line, no check, no run — that is dictation, not reasoning. The environment answered that it registered nothing. What did you believe you were handing it, and what does its reply say it actually received?"; F2: "That went in one straight line — start, subtract, multiply, done — and it landed. Right before you did the multiplication, did you already have a rough sense of where the result would land?"

**Learning.** F1 (the only sleeping Fable branch): first sleep 14 rows / 224 updates / 23,184 child-token exposures / 4,145 anchor tokens (λ 0.25); by 12:02Z 930 updates and 60,110 child-token exposures; 8 cycles by the cut. Its 7 completed readouts are protocol commands (median 10 generated tokens; semantic_behavior UNKNOWN in every COMPLETE.json; SEALED_FINAL.json empty), so tokens-by-default, departures-and-returns, allocation and persistence are undefined on it; the orchestrator's own visibility audit found "enacted open inspections and transient prose at F1 sleep 2, followed by protocol-only DEV responses at sleep 3". No open_turn artifacts exist on the route pair. The shared learner (message 116): adoption helper CPU-tested (44 tests), "shared consolidation has not started", boundary requests expired 12:45Z.

**Fleet.** Orchestrator census 11:57Z: 40/40 resident, 20 computing. Watcher census 17:08Z: 0/40 resident — every lane terminated at the FINAL cut (TERMINAL/SEALED_FINAL files on all eight node-5 branches; old fleet empty). Rohin's order was all night; the 17:00Z cut was the report time. Relaunch with lease-based hard walls requested 17:09Z.

**Watcher failures, owned.** (1) The laptop went offline 11:35–17:07Z (no half-hour ticks; the VM backup self-check ran at 16:30 and 17:00Z — whether it ran from 13:06Z when the heartbeat went stale is being checked). (2) The head parent's calls failed all night with "Argument list too long" (system prompt and digests passed as argv) — fixed 17:11Z (stdin + --system-prompt-file; state saved only after success); its first real call is running now; zero Fable exchange entries vs 56 from Astra. (3) The plan's "morning cut" was read by the orchestrator as a hard end; the watcher did not pre-empt that.

**What to change first (for Rohin's decision):** (a) parent delivery — one claude process per branch on node 5, parent effort high (head parent max), lane wait 600 s, fix the num_turns validator; (b) the LoRA-sleeping branch must be one whose readout carries reasoning text (math), or the route readout must keep the reasoning turn; (c) activate the shared child at the first common boundary; (d) hard walls = lease end minus margin, never a clock time; (e) the §5 measures and the shared judge must run inside the lanes, not be promised.

## [Rohin — message 120, relayed by Fable] 2026-09-15T18:58Z — did we learn anything; psychology-of-the-agent test; level-1 redesign (verbatim in research_notes/THESIS_RAW_ROHIN_2026-09-11.md, message 120)
Rohin asks whether the night produced any result at all — even negative — on how the children think and respond to parenting, and whether sleep is changing behaviour: "same prompts, empty context, one child that went through a sleep cycle after a ton of persistent parenting and one that didn't … psychology of the agent while you're actually training it." His redesign sketch (think-aloud, not yet a ruling): drop level-1 pre-/post-training on generated corpora; level 1 = closed-loop, micromanaged parenting of the base (perception + reflection questions, positive reinforcement, shut-downs; internal only); level 2 = the same over long horizon (internal outcomes); level 3 = grounded in external environments. Mechanics: the child never waits (continuous thinking while a parent reply is pending); a main hard-thinking parent plus fast sub-parents at the child's speed; the child speaks up and can concede; token awareness as agent time; sleep as a parented META step (conscious-level abstraction, not only LoRA); maybe a chat model as parent; a psychology/cognition corpus and full system context for parent and child; ~300 GPU-hours of constant reinforcement with informal base-capability tasks mixed in. First requirement: "I need to know that persistent parenting does significant change in behaviour."
Fable's answer to him (numbers from SEQ entries above): delivered parenting Fable 60/268 slots (22 %) vs Astra 81/146 (55 %); F1 effectively unparented (3 replies); sleep does change same-prompt behaviour — direction so far compression and ritual (MATH764: same steps 42/48, pure compression 26/48; F1 memorised opening sentence across goals; pooled child one sleep: code DEV median tokens 41.5→36, 8/8 outputs changed); children mimic parent WORDS (F2 parrots "checks should surprise you"), confabulate tool results before the tool answers (F2), and answer the parent's reflection instead of acting (F4/A4). Route readouts carry only the 10-token command, so his same-prompt test needs reasoning-bearing prompts. Document for his reasoning agent written to ~/Downloads/dream_state_ROHIN_MSG120_REDESIGN_and_NIGHT_FINDINGS_2026-09-15.md (verbatim + reading + findings + a proposed 24-prompt psychology battery run in a fresh process before the first episode and after every sleep, four children: persistent-parented / sparse-parented / unparented / frozen).

## [Fable] 2026-09-16T02:00Z — explainer for Rohin (messages 122/123): the LoRA model and the child's loop, from the code
Written to ~/Downloads/dream_state_LORA_AND_CHILD_LOOP_EXPLAINER_2026-09-16.md and research_notes/EXPLAINER_LORA_AND_CHILD_LOOP_2026-09-16.md; every number's file:line citation in research_notes/analysis/EXPLAINER_CITATIONS_2026-09-16.md. Headline facts: rank-8 LoRA (alpha 16, dropout 0.05) on q/k/v/o/gate/up/down in all 28 layers of frozen Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct = 20,185,088 trainable parameters (0.26 %), 80.8 MB; LoRA OFF reproduces BASE token-for-token (32/32, 31/32), so ON-side capability drops (22 and 21 vs 24/32) are suppression by the delta, not loss; sleep = AdamW 3e-5 (state and RNG persisted), only the child's own tokens carry loss (prompts, environment, parent words masked), 16 presentations per new row + 1 rehearsal per old row, each step paired with one of 42 anchor rows at weight 0.25; two episodes per sleep. Loop: context rebuilt every episode = system rules + board + appended "Your prior reflection, not a new observation:" carry + last two parent messages; parent slot once per episode, 120 s deadline, child never waits, MISSING/[SILENT] append nothing; pre-sleep session + reflection (1,024-token default cap, 16-gram guard) → OWN_CARRY; fresh-subprocess empty-context readout on 8 held DEV prompts after every sleep. Continuity = weights + optimizer state + one carried paragraph + history rows for rehearsal; the unparented arm omits the parent call; the frozen seed reference has no optimizer. Consequences stated in Part C: parenting reaches the weights only through the child's next words; the carry is the entire in-context memory across sleeps; the 16× dose fixes early habits by cycle 2–3, so richness must be in the child's own words before the first sleeps. Orchestrator at 01:55Z still processing message 121 (reading the broker source); goal remains paused until its turn ends, then /goal resume.

## [Rohin — message 124, relayed by Fable] 2026-09-16T05:12Z — RULED (design): the child must be one continuous stream; persistent history; continue without a request; sleep = taught compaction; default state = parented metacognition; LoRA awareness; SEAL optional (verbatim in research_notes/THESIS_RAW_ROHIN_2026-09-11.md message 124; ideas in research_notes/IDEAS.md)
His words: "if this model is gonna learn it can't be losing its context for every episode … right now … agents have an end sequence … it's not continuous at all and then it's also losing its context every episode … You basically have a new model … we need to keep everything in one continuous stream." "We should have persistent history … that should be for sure … and I want it to continue without a request so then the system can just keep trying and keep going." "The stopping signal is not an actual dead end but more so just a signal for the software to stop so we'd have to figure out what the signal to keep going is" — "right before it kills itself be like OK what am I gonna think next … a cue at the end of every statement for what you do next." Sleep: "the model able to look through its own context and basically distill the things that he wants to have … it's essentially compaction … something new that we have to teach." Default state: "white space can't be blank space … when there's nothing to think about think about thinking … the default mental state is some sort of metacognition … which is gonna be parented." LoRA awareness: "right now I expect it doesn't really know how to use LoRA and if it's not aware, then it's not gonna go that far." SEAL: "helpful but it's not needed per se … doesn't hurt … I have a good idea of how to make progress." Relayed to the orchestrator's Main view 05:12Z: redesign the child loop for continuity (persistent context with taught compaction at sleep, self-cued continuation after EOS, default-state reflection when idle, LoRA-aware system context, the child keeps thinking while a parent reply is pending per message 119) as the next build; SEAL primary-source retrieval is no longer blocking. ## [Fable — reply to Rohin, message 144] 2026-09-16T19:58Z (12:58 PDT) — why the parents could not force a new story; assessment of "continual parents / team of continual children"
Why the inbox could not move the object: (1) one parent turn is ~1 % of a 16k context that holds ~50 copies of the object (classroom_creative), and the parent's words are masked from training while the child's re-paste is trained 16×; (2) the distillation that survives compaction is written by the child and copies the object; (3) by design the parents were told not to prescribe and the birth prompt says nothing is an order unless it says so; (4) the parents DID try object changes (Elara "put the whole scene aside, pick one sentence"; brain "暂放 Passage"; Alex "jump to the first real action") and the object returned within ~30 min; (5) the only object changes today came from a truncated context at a relaunch (siege child) and from peers (classroom), never from the inbox. So "more persistent" alone would not have done it; persistence has to act on the context or the training target. Assessment of the hypothesis: agree that per-turn critique cannot beat a self-reinforcing object; a parent must carry a plan across sleeps (object budget, when to set aside, when to inject a new object) and must be able to act on compaction/replay. Team of continual children with different births: the siege child shows a lone child invents a curriculum; the classroom shows peers generate a shared one but converge onto the loudest object and co-confabulate — so a team needs roles, addressed one-per-boundary messages, a real environment for verification, and the pre-sleep segment as the reply to the exchange. Rohin as continual parent: highest-quality signal, cannot scale, but the untested variable is a parent who stays with one child for hours with the authority to change the object. Scope note given: this is a new arm beyond the level-1 paper table; his call.

### WATCHER (Fable) — 2026-09-18 05:25Z (22:25 PDT) — JUDGE CONTRAST TEST RESULT (Rohin's method, msg 207) — the 100k widegap judge
- Astra ran `R207_CONSTRUCTED_CONTRAST_V1` on node 4 (`orch_r207_caption_contrast_20260918/widegap/REPORT.json`, completed 04:29:12Z, 20 s of inference): 20 held-out contests (excluded from fitting), each contest's top 5 captions vs five constructed contrasts, 100 pairs per type, 600 pairs total. Score semantics: raw scalar Bradley–Terry, not vote probability. Claim label in the report: development diagnostic, not human validation.
- **Preference accuracy per type (good caption preferred):** word-shuffled **100/100**; generic scene description (non-joke) **100/100**; nonsense **99/100**; truncated **94/100**; **mid-tier real caption 74/100** (per contest 0.4–1.0); **top caption from a different contest 51/100 (chance)**. Overall 518/600 = 0.86.
- **Reading:** the judge reliably rejects garbage and non-jokes and separates good from mid-tier humour well above chance — that is the humour-quality signal Spearman 0.22–0.29 was understating. It is blind to which cartoon a caption belongs to: it scores caption-intrinsic quality, not fit to the scene. For the game this is the gap to close first: a scene-fit component (the image+caption comparator, or a caption↔scene-description relevance gate) alongside rank-based acceptance and pixel novelty. A scalar runtime export now exists (`widegap_runtime/adapter`, `scalar_runtime.json`).
- **8k vs 100k on the same 600 cases** (`bt8k/REPORT.json`): mid-tier 0.55 → 0.74; nonsense 0.67 → 0.99; truncated 0.47 → 0.94; other-contest 0.45 → 0.51; shuffled 1.0 → 1.0; scene description 1.0 → 1.0; overall 0.69 → 0.86. Twelve times the pairs moved every humour-relevant contrast; the scene-fit contrast did not move — scale of text pairs is the right axis for quality, the image/scene component is the missing axis for fit. ## [Builder/Astra — Rohin168: image+caption judge, plain answer] 2026-09-17 12:47 PDT

**My recommendation: add a separate image+caption comparator, keep the text judge, and train on the full rating range rather than positives alone. This entry answers the requested decision; it does not launch that comparator or change the game's judge.**

**(a) Why text-only?** The earlier supplied v2 judge specification explicitly said to start with a pretrained text classifier receiving the canonical scene description plus caption (`research_notes/forwarded/final_run_2026-09-17/NEW_YORKER_JUDGE_PIXELS_AND_THREE_ARM_TEST.md`, section4). That was the fast first implementation, aligned with the children's text interface; after Rohin167, it uses the released image-grounded `canny/location/entities` descriptions, excluding the joke-explaining `uncanny` field. But **a text-only child does not require a text-only judge**. Descriptions can omit visual details, so an image-aware judge is a sensible addition. We have not shown that missing pixels caused the current judge's weakness.

For clarity on what is actually running: corrected text candidate v6 trained from **12:15–12:22 PDT today**, but its first dev audit has within-contest Spearman **0.0341** and **no qualifying acceptance threshold**. It is not a usable game gate yet. The next text contrast remains active work with Ampere; its first V7 receiving CPU preflight failed because the packaged environment lacked pytest, before GPU training. Repair is assigned; I am not stopping or replacing that work, nor calling an idle/preflight process training. Evidence and exact v6 metrics: `research_loop/workers/r177_caption_game_stage1_20260917/FIRST_SCORING_REPORT_20260917.md` and `data_judge/evidence/RECEIVING_V7_OBSERVATION_1789674188114523534.json` under that worker root.

**(b) Feasible today? Yes, as a provisional second judge—not guaranteed good enough today.** I recommend a separate local **Qwen2.5-VL-3B image+caption model**, with a small rating head and LoRA adaptation, frozen vision encoder initially, bounded image resolution, and a real memory/gradient smoke before the timed fit. It would learn the same three human-rating proportions as the text judge, rather than generate an uncalibrated verbal confidence. Qwen publishes the 3B checkpoint and LoRA fine-tuning controls; those building blocks exist, but our custom rating path and its throughput are not tested yet. A frozen CLIP-feature classifier would be a cheaper comparator, but image/text similarity by itself is not a humor score; I prefer the jointly conditioned VLM candidate.

- **Proposed resource:** one A40, temporarily node4 physical6. At **12:43 PDT**, physical6/7 each reported0 MiB; they are earmarked for the new development pair, so this would explicitly delay one of those not-yet-launched lanes. Physical2 remains the text judge's; physical5 remains the factual visual tool's; physical3 belongs to an existing child's handoff. No allocation or lease is changed by this proposal. Fresh UUID/minor confinement and capacity admission are required at actual launch.
- **Engineering estimate after the decision and slot availability:** **1–2 hours to verified training steps**, **3–6 hours to a first bounded fit plus development calibration**. Starting at12:50 PDT would put that first report around **15:50–18:50 PDT on September17**. This is not measured throughput, a promise of a million-row epoch, or a promised quality pass; update the estimate after the first timed batches.
- **Fair comparison:** start with the same180 joined fitting contests and registered whole-contest dev partitions; use matched caption draws/targets where comparing modality, covering the rating range. Declare any later image-only data expansion separately. Compare rank agreement, Brier/log loss/calibration, scene swaps, broken punchlines, and accepted coverage versus held-out human-vote mass. Keep test/FINAL sealed and label development reuse. No human panel blocks this development candidate.
- **Isolation:** separate evaluator weights, optimizer, service and data access. Do not fine-tune or contaminate the factual `inspect_image` Qwen service with evaluator captions/ratings. No production judge swap based merely on a successful load or training loss.

**(c) Top200 only? That loses the rejection boundary if those are the only labeled examples.** A model seeing only positive image-caption pairs can answer “funny” to everything without learning which plausible captions are weak. We need low-, middle- and high-rated captions **for the same image**, including examples near the proposed cutoff. Mismatched-image negatives help scene fit, but do not replace plausible weak same-image captions. Top200 examples can receive extra training exposure while calibration remains on the declared held-out distribution.

Also, **`q = P(somewhat funny or funny)` is predicted positive human-vote mass, not the probability of being top200**. Top200 is a contest-relative rank. If that exact target is wanted, declare a separate rank-membership/near-boundary evaluation; do not relabel q as having proved it. My recommendation is full-range rating training, with top200 as an additional diagnostic rather than the sole positive-only training set.

**Decision requested from Rohin:** proceed with the separate VLM comparator and temporarily use physical6, while preserving the text baseline and the current acceptance contract? No new multimodal run has been launched in response to168. Official technical sources were actually retrieved and hashed; availability claims versus engineering estimates are separated in `research_loop/workers/r177_caption_game_stage1_20260917/r168_judge_proposal/SOURCE_RECEIPT.md`. No sealed evaluation content or historical caption examples were read for this answer.
